# omni_default_join_token (Resource)

Points the Omni instance's default join token at an `omni_join_token`. The default is what installation media and machine join configurations use when they name no token of their own, so changing it changes how every such machine joins from then on.

This is a singleton: the instance has exactly one default, which Omni creates at bootstrap and which always exists. Adding this resource therefore adopts the existing setting rather than creating anything, and destroying it leaves whatever token was last set in place, because clearing the default would stop machines joining.

It is the Terraform equivalent of `omnictl jointoken make-default`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omni_join_token" "fleet" {
  name = "fleet"
}

# Make it the instance default: installation media and machine join configurations that name no
# token of their own will use it from here on. Machines that already joined are unaffected.
resource "omni_default_join_token" "this" {
  token_id = omni_join_token.fleet.id
}

# A join configuration with no token selector follows the default, so it picks up the token above.
data "omni_machine_join_config" "default" {
  depends_on = [omni_default_join_token.this]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `token_id` (String, Sensitive) The join token to make the default, i.e. the `id` of an `omni_join_token`. It is the token value itself, so treat it as a credential.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `default`: the Omni instance has a single default join token, so the resource has a fixed ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The instance has exactly one default join token, so the import ID is always `default`. Importing
# reads whatever the instance currently points at.
terraform import omni_default_join_token.this default
```
